AN13-learned-retest.title: Learned-model threat, retested under held-out evaluation
AN13-learned-retest.question: Does a compact learned velocity model help when the test environment was never seen in training, and how much could memorising the public sequences gain?
AN13-learned-retest.method: 1-D CNN (4 conv layers, about 73 k weights) on 1 s windows at 100 Hz (6 channels: gyro and accelerometer as recorded, gaps filled) plus the gravity direction in the body frame from the X108b attitude, body-frame velocity target from ground truth, heteroscedastic Gaussian NLL, AdamW + one-cycle, 14 epochs, trained on TRAIN missions (seeds 5001-5004) and tested on DEV missions (seeds 1001-1004); folds: leave-one-environment-out for EuRoC (MH, V1, V2) and leave-one-room-out for TUM-VI (room1-6); predictions fused into X108b as world-frame velocity rows with the predicted variance x s^2 (s = 1, 2, 4, 8) wherever no zero-velocity row exists; DEV (136 missions) vs X108b, paired bootstrap over sequences. In-pool folds (trained on the test missions) measure memorisation only.
AN13-learned-retest.result: Held-out velocity RMSE (m/s), net / estimator / zero: MH 0.81/0.32/0.92, V1 0.58/0.23/0.80, V2 0.61/0.27/0.70, rooms 0.67-0.98/0.10-0.18/0.56-1.13 (worse than zero in room4 and room6); predicted 3-D sigma 0.23-0.46 (over-confident: 3-D RMS error / sigma = 1.3-3.2). Fusion, held-out: s1 +53.7 %, s2 +26.4 %, s4 +9.0 % [+3.6, +15.9], s8 +2.6 % [-0.8, +5.9] composite (always worse; TUM-VI +30 to +264 %). In-pool: s1 +5.1 %, s2 -7.9 %, s4 -9.3 % [-13.4, -6.0] (EuRoC -8.2 %, TUM-VI -20.9 %), s8 -5.0 %. Runtime +55-75 % (side-file lookups in the smoother loop).
AN13-learned-retest.decision: No learned component: with this data (11 flights, 6 rooms) the model does not transfer to an unseen environment at any weighting. The memorisation threat is bounded at about -9 % composite on DEV for this model class and would require the hidden data to be the public sequences; it is not admissible for us (sequence memorisation is excluded by our rules).

AN25-drag-offset-wander.title: Does the wander of the loose drag-row offset tell when the steady prior helps?
AN25-drag-offset-wander.question: Can a statistic of the loose solution (rather than its radius) choose the steady drag prior, so that MH_01 (radius 1.3-1.5 m, never switched) also gains and the T4 misfires are avoided?
AN25-drag-offset-wander.method: main_dev K, loose prior only (switch off) with the smoother states recorded vs steady prior forced, on DEV (88 EuRoC missions) and E46 seed 0 (319 rotor cases); S = RMS deviation of the 10 s moving average of the two drag-row offsets over flight blocks; rules compared by the mean ATE of the chosen solution (notes/an25b_rules.py)
AN25-drag-offset-wander.result: Official DEV: S is large on Machine Hall flights (0.041-0.123) where the steady prior helps (MH_01 -5..-24 %, MH_03-05 -14..-41 %) and small in the Vicon rooms (0.014-0.052) where it is neutral or harmful (V1_03 +14..+60 %). Rule S >= 0.040-0.045: -14.8 % vs loose (radius rule -13.0 %, always steady -13.2 %, oracle -15.6 %), but MH_03 (0.045-0.077) and the V tail (up to 0.052) overlap, so the threshold is a knife-edge. E46 stress: accelerometer ramps make S large in the V rooms and the S rule switches them (acc_ramp_1 V1_03 +308 %, V2_02 +181 %, V2_01 +150 %): mean -1.3 % vs -3.2 % for the radius rule, 47 vs 30 bad choices; hybrids (radius or S with a radius floor) keep the acc_ramp failures.
AN25-drag-offset-wander.decision: Not adopted: the statistic is environment-learned and brittle under unmodelled drifts; the radius rule stays. Documented for future work (a drift-aware statistic that tells real offset drift from absorbed velocity)
